newsitem.title: USA: Belgian carrier City Bird to land in Miami.
newsitem.headline: Belgian carrier City Bird to land in Miami.

text.p: Belgian carrier CityBird will begin non-stop full-service flights on Wednesdays and Sundays from Miami to Brussels on March 30, with one-way fares as low as $149 good through June 22, the airline announced Friday.
The carrier is offering an introductory one-way fare for the first three flights of $99, Trevor Sadler, director of operations said Friday.
Currently, American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp and Delta Air Lines serve Brussels from Miami.
CityBird flies McDonnel-Douglas MD-11 widebody aircraft with business class and economy class.

"CityBird is giving customers what they want -- affordable fares to Europe with quality in-flight services and comfort," Chairman Victor Hasson said in a statement. The fares feature electronic ticketing and limited restrictions. Round-trip purchase is not required and there is no minimum stay.

CityBird will also start non-stop service from Brussels to Mexico City on March 27. It will begin four flights weekly from Newark on June 2. Los Angeles will get twice per week service from June 3 and San Francisco weekly from June 7.
CityBird is a subsidiary of City Hotels SA, Brussles. The U.S. headquarters is in Bethesda Maryland.
